subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should the surviving WhatsApp image active_reply_work loop be fixed at terminal reply ownership cleanup, at stuck-session recovery for aborted/released=0 outcomes, or folded into the broader WhatsApp replay-storm tracker?
rationale: The reporter's v2026.6.10 repro contradicts the assumption that the earlier lane-release fix fully solved this class, and the safe fix boundary changes when OpenClaw is allowed to clear an apparently active embedded reply owner.

options.title: Keep separate and require live proof
options.body: Treat this as a distinct surviving recovery bug, gather redacted live WhatsApp proof on current main or v2026.6.11, then choose the narrow owner-boundary fix.

options.title: Fold into the broader WhatsApp tracker
options.body: Move the remaining discussion under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97538 only if maintainers decide the direct-image loop shares the same owner-lock/replay root cause.

options.title: Queue a recovery fix now
options.body: Let an automated repair attempt a guarded recovery change for aborted/released=0 active_reply_work outcomes, accepting that live WhatsApp proof may come after the code path fix.

recommendation.title: Keep separate and require live proof
recommendation.body: Treat this as a distinct surviving recovery bug, gather redacted live WhatsApp proof on current main or v2026.6.11, then choose the narrow owner-boundary fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the clearest maintainer-side routing signal from prior recovery closure context and current-source ownership in this checkout.
